---
title: "Forest Management"
---

iLand includes two subsystems that handle forest management:

* **"Base" management:** A simple, versatile scripting approach that allows altering the forest directly through JavaScript (harvesting trees, planting, modifying soil carbon, etc.).
* **[Agent-Based Management Engine (ABE)](abe.qmd):** A powerful module that simulates multiple management agents across a landscape. Agents can react to changes in the environment by adapting management plans and executing dynamically scheduled activities.

Choosing between these management approaches is handled by keys in the [project file](project-file.qmd):

* To use **base management**: set `model.management.enabled` to `true` and `model.management.abeEnabled` to `false` in the [management](project-file-reference.qmd#management) section.
* To use **ABE**: set `model.management.enabled` to `false` and `model.management.abeEnabled` to `true` in the [management](project-file-reference.qmd#management) section (it is technically possible to enable both mechanisms at the same time).

## Base Management Scripting

The management approach in iLand relies on JavaScript as the scripting language. The model exposes a rich set of objects and functions allowing a management script to interact directly with the forest:

* Good starting points in the API documentation are the **[Management API](../apidoc/classes/iland/management.qmd)** and **[Globals API](../apidoc/classes/iland/globals.qmd)**.
* Additional core scripting objects include **[Map](../apidoc/classes/iland/map.qmd)** (for GIS raster stands) and **[CSVFile](../apidoc/classes/iland/csvfile.qmd)** (for reading input data tables).

In base management, a single JavaScript file is defined in the [Project file](project-file.qmd) (setting `model.management.file`) and loaded during model startup. Every simulation year, the function `manage()` is called automatically by iLand:

```javascript
function manage(year)
{
    print('management called in year ' + year);
}
```

The user provides their own logic for dispatching events over time. Several complete scripting examples demonstrate how this is done:

* **[Parallel Management](management-example-parallel-management.qmd)**: Demonstrates handling parallel, stand-level events over time.
* **[HJA Fire History](management-example-hja-fire-history.qmd)**: Shows how to reconstruct historical fire and harvest events across a landscape.
* **[Restoration Area (Modern JavaScript)](management-example-restoration-area-modern-javascript.qmd)**: Illustrates how to read custom tabular data files (such as CSVs), filter and manipulate data in memory, and dynamically execute operations (like planting) based on it.

::: {.callout-note}
In the annual [simulation sequence](simulation-sequence.qmd), management operations are executed early in the year, before growth, mortality, and disturbance modules run.
:::
